newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest runoff forecasts trimmed slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest runoff forecasts trimmed slightly.

text.p: The Northwest River Forecast Center's latest update of spring runoff forecasts for hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest calls for levels slightly lower than earlier near-record forecasts.

In its mid-February assessement, the center forecast January to July runoff on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam in Oregon at 132 percent of average, compared with an estimate in early February of 137 percent.
Last year runoff at The Dalles during the same period came in at 132 percent of average, near 140 million acre feet (maf).

April to July inflow to the Brownlee reservoir on the Snake River in Idaho was forecast at a revised 101 maf or 174 percent of average rates, compared with the early February forecast of 190 percent of average.
The January-July inflow forecast for the Lower Granite reservoir on the Snake in Washington was lowered to 153 percent of average from 165 percent in the earlier estimate.
